articles.title: Hands-on Impressions of Hoid's Storybook Collection by Brandon Sanderson
articles.summary: Cosmere fans rejoice! The latest Brandon Sanderson Cosmere book, as a part of Hoid’s Storybook Collection, has started arriving for BackerKit backers. I had backed at the Storyteller tier when the campaign first launched and received my ebooks, PDFs, and audiobook all at once on Sept. 15.
body: Here are my initial impressions on the latest BackerKit campaign from Dragonsteel.

The Fires of December is the third book in what Sanderson is calling Hoid’s Travails. Fans of Tress of the Emerald Sea and Yumi and the Nightmare Painter (the other two stories in Hoid’s Travails) will want to get their hands on December right away. It is a standalone Cosmere book in a sense. December, the protagonist, is on a new planet in the Cosmere with her own plot and storyline. Where it connects to the Tress and Yumi is the narrator of the book is everyone’s favorite Worldhopper, Hoid.
points: The latest Brandon Sanderson Cosmere book, as a part of Hoid’s Storybook Collection, has started arriving for BackerKit backers.

articles.title: Star Citizen Single-Player Spinoff Squadron 42 Reemerges With Flashy New Trailer, Steam Wishlists, and Cast Confirmation
articles.summary: Star Citizen developer Cloud Imperium Games has pulled back the curtain on single-player spinoff Squadron 42 with a new cinematic trailer, the launch of Steam wishlists, and a full cast reveal.
body: Squadron 42 is the story-driven off-shoot of space sim Star Citizen, which Cloud Imperium Games has worked on for the last 12 years. Its 12-year development is led by Chris Roberts, creator of the Wing Commander series. Indeed, Squadron 42 is a spiritual successor to Wing Commander, and like the Wing Commander games, Squadron 42 features a string of Hollywood stars, such as Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Gillian Anderson, Ben Mendelsohn, and Henry Cavill.

The game fuses space combat, first-person shooter action, and a character-driven narrative supported by full performance capture. CIG said the performances are woven directly into gameplay, so you won’t just see those famous actors within cinematics.

articles.title: WandaVision Creator Set To Develop New Stargate Series
articles.summary: After a failed attempt, Amazon MGM Studios is once again developing a Stargate series. According to Variety, the company is bringing on Jac Schaeffer, the showrunner of one of Disney Plus's most successful shows, WandaVision.
body: Amazon has wanted to create a Stargate TV series for a while now. Martin Gero, creator of Blindspot, had worked on various Stargate television series early in his career, so bringing him on board for a new series felt like the right move in 2025. Unfortunately, the project was canceled early in development.

According to Variety, Amazon was "concerned that Gero's take on the series would not have broad appeal." Despite these setbacks, Amazon wasn't ready to give up and was still on the prowl for a writer, and it seems it might've just found her.

Earlier this year, the company made a three-year deal with Jac Schaeffer. It is now taking advantage of the deal by handing her the Stargate project. You likely know Schaeffer best for her work as the creator of WandaVision and Agatha All Along, two critically acclaimed shows that reached the top of the charts on Disney Plus. Clearly, Amazon is hoping she can replicate that success with a Stargate show.

Very little is known about this project or how it differs from what Gero's take would've been. Regardless, Schaeffer will surely put her spin on the project and make it the best she possibly can for today's viewership.

According to Variety, the company is bringing on Jac Schaeffer, the showrunner of one of Disney Plus's most successful shows, WandaVision.

articles.title: Ray Gunn Review
articles.summary: Director Brad Bird’s Ray Gunn is a love letter to film noir and old-school science fiction, beautifully bringing its retro-futuristic world to life with great style and attention to detail.
body: Ray Gunn opens in select theaters on December 4 and arrives on Netflix on December 18. The film premiered on October 10 at the London Film Festival.

A 30-odd-year passion project for director Brad Bird, Ray Gunn is a nifty sci-fi/film noir mashup that’s sumptuously designed and cleverly realized, but is slightly dinged by an overlong runtime and occasionally clunky story.

Set in the vast futuristic city of Metropia, Ray Gunn follows its titular private eye (voiced by Sam Rockwell) as he and his one-eyed alien partner, Eye-Ra (Tom Waits), investigate a case involving the world’s biggest pop star, Venus Nova (Scarlett Johansson), that leads to murder, corruption and other nefarious things. If that sounds pretty gritty for an animated film from the director of The Incredibles and Ratatouille, it is.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Story Recap – What You Need To Know Ahead of MW4
articles.summary: The whole story of Call of Duty's rebooted Modern Warfare saga ends in this month's MW4. Catch up on everything you need to know before you play, including all the stuff that happened in Warzone's cutscenes.
body: It’s fair to say that, across the three games in the reboot series so far, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare’s story has been far from a simple one. With the amount of action happening during each mission, combined with key plot points occurring outside of the core campaigns in places like Warzone’s Verdansk, it can be difficult to keep track.

Thankfully, we’re here to give you as succinct a summary as we can of the story so far ahead of Modern Warfare 4 ’s release. With Infinity Ward’s saga set to come to an end imminently, let’s recap how we got here. Warning: may contain a lot of chasing stolen missiles around the world.

2019’s Modern Warfare reboot tells the story of Task Force 141’s creation. That’s the elite team of operatives helmed by Call of Duty veteran Captain John Price (but not the same John Price who was in the original Modern Warfare, nor the John Price who was in the original two Call of Dutys. Look, we did say this was complicated).

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens is a brilliant take-down of Korra's biggest haters
articles.summary: The Korra series finale — as later seen in high-definition under normal connection speeds — is still one of my favorite endings (and favorite TV shows) of all time. But it’s hard to ignore the flaws; from a slashed budget that forced the animators to rely on still images for some pivotal scenes…
body: At the stroke of midnight on Dec. 19, 2014, Nickelodeon unceremoniously dumped the final two episodes of Avatar: The Legend of Korra on Nick.com. That night, I gathered on the couch with my roommate to witness the culmination of an epic four-season story. Unfortunately, 2014 streaming technology still had a long ways to go, and after watching Nickelodeon's online video player buffer for about 15 minutes, I gave up and went to bed. It was Thursday night, and I had work in the morning.

Seven Havens takes place over 200 years after Legend of Korra. A mysterious calamity has undone the industrial revolution that escalated across the previous two shows. Instead of the gleaming, utopian Republic City in Korra, or even the sprawling, walled kingdom of Ba Sing Se in The Last Airbender, there are seven fortified "havens" spread across this world, with seemingly nothing but inhospitable desert in between. Some time after the Four Nations invented hoverbikes, everything collapsed.

articles.title: I Have Discovered The Best Game Soundtrack of 2026 and It Is Super Woden: Rally Edge
articles.summary: Video game soundtracks are pretty respectable these days. Earlier this year, I watched James Bond composer David Arnold take the stage at the BAFTA Games Awards and pay tribute to the medium before presenting an award to Toma Otowa for the Ghost of Yōtei soundtrack.
body: It's mostly high-energy stuff, as befits a game about sending toylike cars hurtling and powersliding along two-minute rally stages. It's also quite retro, as befits a game with a kind of cel-shaded PS1 aesthetic. It consists of EDM, metal, hip-hop, and jazz-funk rendered with a synthetic MIDI sound that pairs naturally with vibrant low-poly graphics and blocky, functional menus.

It's a soundtrack of two halves, provided by two different artists. DJ DeVito provides the spine: a suite of techno, Eurodance, electro, and happy hardcore, all of it relentlessly and joyously upbeat. "Drive or Die" is infectiously jolly, powered by an insistent bassline and amusingly 80s synthesized orchestra stabs. "Across the Universe" is another example of DJ DeVito's hilariously insistent four-to-the-floor techno.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

This solid foundation is then built on by the work of a true wizard called DonutDroid who puts the Super Woden: Rally Edge soundtrack on a whole new level. DonutDroid's ability to flit between musical genres while maintaining a consistent sound and vibe is truly amazing.

articles.title: Silent Hill, Gravity Rush director's Bokeh Game Studio is reportedly casting for a new horror game
articles.summary: It looks like Bokeh Game Studio, founded by Keiichiro Toyama, who directed the original Silent Hill and created Siren and Gravity Rush, is working on another horror game.
body: According to MP1st, Bokeh is hiring motion capture performers for its next project, which is seemingly still untitled.
The casting sheet lists characters including River, Dean, Lyra, Hazel, Becca, Dena, and Emma, plus an eight-year-old girl.

Descriptions cover mature themes including drug use and trafficking, violence, abuse, grief, and sex work, with several characters tied to creature transformation - all of which sounds surprisingly close to Toyama's prior game, Slitterhead… which is interesting, given Slitterhead didn't exactly set the world alight.
River's entry cites River Phoenix and Kurt Cobain as visual references, while Lyra's points to Mia Goth as a tonal reference.

articles.title: Grand Theft Ocarina Could Be Gaming's Barbenheimer
articles.summary: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.
body: Making games gets harder, longer, and more expensive every year, but nobody seems to have told Nintendo. The platform-holder has kept up a schedule of more-or-less monthly new exclusives all year, and it's been a lineup of impressive breadth and quality.

Three weeks have passed since the massive Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and only two weeks are left until Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. Time for the hands-on previews, then, and Polygon's Mike McWhertor duly reports that Switch Sports Resort is a perfectly chill compilation that channels WaveRace, Pilotwings, and even Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, as well as the mighty Wii Sports.

We all know this is just the build-up, though. Just two weeks after Switch Sports Resort comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, a remake so consequential, of a game so revered, that it effectively has the status of a brand-new mainline Zelda game. I've heard a plausible but unverified rumor that this is how it's being treated internally; that, rather than entrust the remake to an outside developer like Grezzo (which handled Ocarina of Time 3D and the Link's Awakening remake), Nintendo made it in-house.
points: Making games gets harder, longer, and more expensive every year, but nobody seems to have told Nintendo.
The platform-holder has kept up a schedule of more-or-less monthly new exclusives all year, and it's been a lineup of impressive breadth and quality.

articles.title: Triple-A Minesweeper is a gleeful send-up of blockbuster gaming's worst habits, from yellow paint to characters who talk too much
articles.summary: In recent years, triple-A games have often been criticised for overly excessive handholding, overcompensating for a dread fear that the player might become stuck. This has manifested in numerous ways like Atreus' heavy-handed puzzle hints in God of War: Ragnarok, yellow paint splashed on every…
body: I'm not here to weigh in on that debate. Instead, I'm simply going to point you to Triple-A Minesweeper, a delightful spoof game created by developer Mike Lacher, which expertly skewers some of blockbuster gaming's most egregious habits.

Now, before I describe the experience of playing Triple-A Minesweeper, I strongly suggest that you go and play it. It only takes about five minutes, so in explaining it I will probably tell you about most of the game. It should also give you a giggle, perhaps several, even!

But if you insist on reading on, then unlike regular Minesweeper, which begins by letting you play Minesweeper, Triple-A Minesweeper opens with a bunch of un-skippable title cards for third-party software and developers, before we get the dramatic title of the game itself. Then your character—the Sweeper—slowly blinks open his eyes as a woman called Nora fills you in on the situation, namely that you need to sweep some mines.

articles.title: The advent of first-person shooters introduced a wild frontier of unregulated video game level packs, and it ended in a lawsuit that changed copyright forever
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh and Rick have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager.

For most of PC gaming history, there were three states of PC game—your regular old video game, expansions/DLC, and mods. But for a brief period in the 1990s, there was a fourth state, the level pack—collections of levels for the early first-person shooters like Duke Nukem 3D and Quake.

These level packs were sold on shelves as boxed products just like their video game counterparts. But they occupied a far more amorphous position between the other three states of PC gaming. In form and structure, they were similar to expansions, and are sometimes bundled into the same category. The Master Levels for Doom 2, for example, are regarded as an official expansion to that game.
points: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom.

articles.title: Expect plenty more Silent Hill over the next few years, as Konami has plans for 'second and third waves' of new games in its revived horror series
articles.summary: Silent Hill's resurrection is one of the happier stories to emerge from the games industry in recent years. After spending roughly a decade locked in a Konami cupboard, Silent Hill has received three new entries published by Konami in as many years, all of which arrived to positive reviews and…
body: In an interview featured in Famitsu (via IGN ), Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto explained that Konami is "relieved" by both the critical and commercial reception to the aforementioned three games. "All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully," Okamoto said, adding that, "they've also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it."

Okamoto went on to say that the games released so far only represent the "first wave" of Konami's planned games for the series, and that there's not one but two additional waves on the drawing board. "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we're not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves," Okamoto stated. "We can't share specific details, but we're currently looking at a number of projects."

It's a very different situation from where Silent Hill was only a few years ago. During the chat, Okamoto revealed that persuading Konami's executive to pursue new entries in the series has been challenging, especially after the cancellation of Hideo Kojima's Silent Hills in 2015.
points: Silent Hill's resurrection is one of the happier stories to emerge from the games industry in recent years.

articles.title: 'If you're skilful enough, you can chop the head off a monster, kick it midair, and then kill another monster with it': Consider me sold on this indie first-person ARPG
articles.summary: Certain ideas that crop up every so often in games will always grab my attention. One of them is letting players defeat enemies with bits of other enemies. As such, my interest in Heathen—an upcoming indie dungeon crawler—went from 'mildly curious' to 'smashing the wishlist button' when its most…
body: Developed by solo developer Christoper Yabsley, Heathen takes the frantic monster bashing and loot hoarding of Diablo and reworks it for a first-person perspective. Set in the fantasy town of Saltgrave, it sees your character seeking fortune and glory in the vast subterranean labyrinth beneath the town, encountering an "ancient horror" in the process in what the Steam page describes as a "descent into madness."

The chief addition that the trailer explores is a new enemy dismemberment system added by Yabsley, which he says has "done a lot for making swords and axes feel really good". As a longtime fan of first-person melee games like Dark Messiah of Might and Magic and Warhammer: Vermintide 2 (the latter of which is an influence on Heathen's combat), I'm highly impressed by how slick and tactile Heathen's combat looks. It isn't easy to make first-person swordplay satisfying—especially as a solo indie dev—and Heathen's fast-paced hacking and slashing makes an excellent initial impression.
points: Certain ideas that crop up every so often in games will always grab my attention.
One of them is letting players defeat enemies with bits of other enemies.

Having already delivered the Complete Edition, CD Projekt RED still has plans for The Witcher 3, hence the arrival of the controversial Remastered release - and while it has some key improvements, there are still some issues. In our PC performance review, we present the top-line changes to the game then compare the hotfix 5.00C version to the latest patch 5.01 before we dive head-first into those all-important optimised settings.

videos.title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort – Overview Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: The Nintendo Switch Sports Resort game launches October 22, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2 system. Pre-orders are available now:
body: The latest game in the intuitive sports series is coming to Nintendo Switch 2!
Get moving solo or with family and friends across 12 immersive sports. Aim for the target’s center in Archery, knock down pins in Bowling, duke it out in Boxing, and more!
You can also explore the island! Use Joy-Con 2 mouse controls in Skateboarding, steer across the waves in Power Cruising, and tilt the controller to fly around freely in Prop Plane.

videos.summary: Valor Mortis releases on October 13th. Valor Mortis is a first-person action soulslike from the creators of Ghostrunner. Rise from death as a former soldier of Napoleon’s army. Wield supernatural powers, battle horrifying monsters, and unravel a conspiracy that threatens all of humanity.
